questions.text: What is the main limitation of greedy decoding for text generation?
options: It requires too much memory
It cannot process long sequences
It always picks the highest-probability token, producing repetitive and predictable text
It requires a special tokenizer
questions.explanation: Greedy decoding selects the argmax token at every step. This deterministic approach often falls into repetitive loops and misses globally better sequences that start with a lower-probability token.

questions.text: How does the temperature parameter affect the softmax distribution during generation?
options: Higher temperature makes the distribution sharper (more confident)
Higher temperature flattens the distribution, increasing randomness and diversity
Temperature only affects the first token in a sequence
Temperature controls the maximum sequence length
questions.explanation: Temperature T divides logits before softmax: softmax(z/T). Higher T flattens the distribution (more uniform, more random), while lower T sharpens it (approaching greedy as T→0).

questions.text: What does top-p (nucleus) sampling do differently from top-k sampling?
options: Top-p always selects exactly p tokens
Top-p ignores the probability distribution entirely
Top-p uses a fixed number of candidates regardless of distribution shape
Top-p dynamically adjusts the candidate set size based on cumulative probability, adapting to distribution shape
questions.explanation: Top-p selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p. When the model is confident (peaked distribution), fewer tokens are included; when uncertain, more tokens are considered. This adapts to context unlike fixed top-k.

questions.text: Which strategies can help reduce repetition in generated text?Select all that apply
options: Repetition penalty that reduces the probability of previously generated tokens
Setting temperature to 0
Using only greedy decoding
Increasing temperature or using nucleus sampling to introduce diversity
questions.explanation: Repetition penalty explicitly penalizes tokens that already appeared in the output. Increasing temperature or using nucleus sampling introduces stochasticity. Setting temperature to 0 or using greedy decoding actually increases repetition.

questions.text: In beam search with beam width B, how many candidate sequences are maintained at each step?
options: B sequences, keeping the top-B by cumulative log-probability
B² sequences, squaring the beam width each step
All possible sequences are kept and pruned at the end
Only 1 sequence, but B tokens are sampled per step
questions.explanation: Beam search maintains exactly B candidate hypotheses. At each step, each beam is extended by all vocabulary tokens, then only the top-B expansions (by cumulative log-probability) are kept. This explores multiple paths without exhaustive search.
